services/api/horolog/domain/time.py::min.detail: Raises ValueError on negative input; 20 min with 15-min slots yields 2, never 1. The `-(-a // b)` idiom is integer ceiling division.

services/api/horolog/domain/time.py::slo.detail: Exact inverse of minutes_to_slots only for multiples of SLOT_MINUTES. Round-tripping 20 minutes returns 30.

services/api/horolog/domain/time.py::to_.oneLiner: Floors an absolute datetime to a slot index
services/api/horolog/domain/time.py::to_.detail: Both args must be timezone-aware or it raises ValueError; returns a signed index, negative when moment precedes origin. Floor division on total_seconds, so sub-slot remainders are dropped.

services/api/horolog/domain/time.py::fro.oneLiner: Converts a slot index back to a datetime
services/api/horolog/domain/time.py::fro.detail: Returns origin shifted by slot * SLOT_MINUTES, inheriting origin's tzinfo. No tz-awareness check here, unlike to_slot; arithmetic is wall-clock via timedelta, so DST shifts are not absorbed.

services/api/horolog/domain/time.py::day.oneLiner: Maps a slot index to its day index
services/api/horolog/domain/time.py::day.detail: Floor division by SLOTS_PER_DAY, counted from the horizon origin. Negative slots floor toward -inf, so slot -1 is day -1.

services/api/horolog/domain/time.py::day.oneLiner: First slot index of a given day
services/api/horolog/domain/time.py::day.detail: Left inverse of day_of: day_of(day_start(d)) == d. Day d spans slots day_start(d) through day_start(d+1) - 1.

services/api/horolog/domain/intent.py::P.oneLiner: P1..P4 int enum, lower = more important
services/api/horolog/domain/intent.py::P.detail: IntEnum so it compares and sorts numerically; P1=1 is critical, P4=4 is low. Matches Reclaim's priority numbering.

services/api/horolog/domain/intent.py::I.detail: StrEnum with task, habit, focus, buffer, meeting — serializes as the raw string. Tags what kind of time demand an Intent is; carries no behavior.

services/api/horolog/domain/intent.py::D.oneLiner: Allowed time-of-day range in minutes from midnight
services/api/horolog/domain/intent.py::D.detail: start_min/end_min both clamped to 0..1440 by Pydantic Field bounds. Validates start < end, so it cannot express a window crossing midnight — split into two windows for that.
Pydantic mode="after" model validator; raises ValueError on zero-length or inverted ranges, otherwise returns self. Runs on every construction, including model_validate.

services/api/horolog/domain/intent.py::I.oneLiner: One time demand the solver must schedule
services/api/horolog/domain/intent.py::I.detail: Holds volume (minutes_per_period), recurrence (period_days: None = one-shot, 7 = weekly), chunk size bounds, per-day cap, allowed daily windows, slot-index earliest/due bounds, and a soft preferred_start_min. All minute fields must be SLOT_MINUTES multiples; the *_slots properties convert them for the solver.

services/api/horolog/domain/intent.py::I.oneLiner: Rejects Intents that could never be scheduled
services/api/horolog/domain/intent.py::I.detail: Checks max_chunk >= min_chunk, minutes_per_period >= min_chunk, all three minute fields divisible by SLOT_MINUTES, due_slot > earliest_slot when both set, and every daily_window at least min_chunk wide. Raises ValueError with a message naming the offending field; does not check max_per_day or feasibility against total calendar capacity.
Property wrapping minutes_to_slots. Safe because _coherent already enforced SLOT_MINUTES divisibility.
Property wrapping minutes_to_slots. Lower bound on the length of any placed block.
Property wrapping minutes_to_slots. Upper bound on the length of any placed block.

services/api/horolog/domain/events.py::T.oneLiner: StrEnum: free vs busy time marking
services/api/horolog/domain/events.py::T.detail: Two members, FREE and BUSY, with string values "free"/"busy". StrEnum means members compare equal to and serialize as those strings, so JSON round-trips without conversion.

services/api/horolog/domain/events.py::B.oneLiner: Immovable time block the solver can't schedule over
services/api/horolog/domain/events.py::B.detail: Pydantic model with source_id, half-open slot range [start_slot, end_slot), and optional label; start_slot must be >= 0. Covers both external calendar events and locked internal blocks — the solver treats both as hard constraints, so nothing schedules on top.
Pydantic mode="after" model validator; raises ValueError on empty or inverted ranges, otherwise returns self. Rejects zero-length intervals (end == start), not just negative ones.

services/api/horolog/domain/plan.py::Sol.detail: StrEnum, so members compare and serialize as plain strings. INFEASIBLE only fires on contradictory hard constraints (overlapping locked blocks); a calendar with too little free time still solves and reports UnmetDemand instead.

services/api/horolog/domain/plan.py::Sch.oneLiner: One placed chunk of work on the slot timeline
services/api/horolog/domain/plan.py::Sch.detail: Identified by (intent_id, occurrence, chunk); occupies half-open slot range [start_slot, end_slot). moved_from carries its start slot in the prior plan, None if new; validation rejects zero-length or reversed ranges.
Pydantic mode='after' model validator; raises ValueError on empty or inverted ranges. Zero-length blocks are rejected, not just negative ones.
Property returning the block's stable identity across replans, independent of where it landed. Used to diff a new plan against the old one.
Property, end_slot - start_slot. Always >= 1 given the validator.

services/api/horolog/domain/plan.py::Unm.oneLiner: Requested time the solver could not place
services/api/horolog/domain/plan.py::Unm.detail: Per (intent_id, occurrence), records required_slots vs placed_slots and the priority that lost. Emitted on FEASIBLE solves rather than raising, so an over-subscribed week surfaces to the user.

services/api/horolog/domain/plan.py::Unm.oneLiner: Slots still missing: required minus placed
services/api/horolog/domain/plan.py::Unm.detail: Property. Zero would mean fully satisfied, so such entries shouldn't appear in the list.

services/api/horolog/domain/plan.py::Pla.detail: Pydantic model holding scheduled blocks, demands that didn't fit, solve time in ms, and horizon length in slots. No status field by design — infeasibility is expressed as entries in `unmet`, not a flag, so an empty `blocks` list with a full `unmet` list is still a valid Plan.
Builds a fresh dict on each call — no caching, so hoist it out of loops. Duplicate keys would silently collapse.

services/api/horolog/domain/plan.py::Pla.oneLiner: Total slot distance blocks moved since prior plan
services/api/horolog/domain/plan.py::Pla.detail: Sums abs(start_slot - moved_from) over blocks that have moved_from; new blocks contribute nothing. Exposes the objective's minimal-perturbation term as a stability metric.

services/api/horolog/solver/expand.py::A.oneLiner: Half-open absolute slot range [lo,hi) inside a single day
services/api/horolog/solver/expand.py::A.detail: Pydantic model holding lo, hi (absolute slot indices) and the day index they belong to. Never spans midnight — day-crossing time is split into separate windows by _windows_for.
Returns hi - lo. No units conversion; slots, not minutes.

services/api/horolog/solver/expand.py::R.oneLiner: One occurrence of one intent's demand, ready for the solver
services/api/horolog/solver/expand.py::R.detail: Flattens an Intent into a single period's demand: slot counts, chunk bounds, per-day cap, candidate windows, deadline, preferred start offset. All time fields are slots; preferred_offset is slots from midnight, not absolute.

services/api/horolog/solver/expand.py::R.oneLiner: Number of chunk variables the solver should allocate
services/api/horolog/solver/expand.py::R.detail: required_slots // min_chunk, clamped to [1, MAX_CHUNKS_PER_REQUIREMENT]. Floor is 1 even when required_slots < min_chunk, so the count can exceed what the requirement can actually hold in that edge case.

services/api/horolog/solver/expand.py::R.oneLiner: Total slots available across all windows
services/api/horolog/solver/expand.py::R.detail: Sums window spans as a cheap upper bound — capacity_slots < required_slots means infeasible. Ignores contention with other requirements, so passing it proves nothing.

services/api/horolog/solver/expand.py::_.oneLiner: Clip an intent's daily windows onto absolute range [lo,hi)
services/api/horolog/solver/expand.py::_.detail: Emits one AllowedWindow per (day × daily_window) intersected with [lo,hi); no daily_windows means the full day. Drops any result shorter than intent.min_chunk_slots, and returns [] when hi <= lo — so an empty list means unschedulable, not unbounded.

services/api/horolog/solver/expand.py::e.oneLiner: Fans one Intent out into per-period Requirement rows
services/api/horolog/solver/expand.py::e.detail: No period_days yields at most one Requirement spanning [earliest_slot, horizon); otherwise one per whole period that fits, each searching at most SCHEDULING_RANGE_DAYS ahead. Pure function; periods with no candidate windows are dropped silently and a trailing partial period is never emitted.

services/api/horolog/solver/expand.py::e.oneLiner: expand() over a list of intents, flattened
services/api/horolog/solver/expand.py::e.detail: Concatenates expand(intent, horizon_slots) for every intent. No dedup, no ordering guarantee beyond input order.

services/api/horolog/solver/model.py::We.oneLiner: Objective coefficients for the CP-SAT scheduler.
services/api/horolog/solver/model.py::We.detail: Pydantic model holding the reward per slot by priority (`place`), the kind tiebreak, and penalties for fragmentation, movement (`perturb`, capped at `perturb_cap`), lateness, and time-of-day deviation. The place/perturb ratio is what produces preemption and plan stability — there is no rule for either, only these numbers, and the validator refuses combinations that invert the intended ordering.

services/api/horolog/solver/model.py::We.oneLiner: Rejects weight sets that break the objective's ordering.
services/api/horolog/solver/model.py::We.detail: Runs after model init and raises ValueError on three conditions: cheapest `place` <= `fragment` (solver paid to drop low-priority work), `kind_tiebreak * max(KIND_RANK)` >= the smallest gap between priority tiers (kind outranks priority), or `perturb * perturb_cap` >= `cheapest * _MIN_SANE_CHUNK_SLOTS` (stability outranks scheduling). Returns self so Pydantic keeps the instance.

services/api/horolog/solver/model.py::Ch.oneLiner: CP-SAT variables for one chunk of one requirement
services/api/horolog/solver/model.py::Ch.detail: Holds present (bool), start/end/size ints, and window_lits — one bool per candidate window, exactly one of which is true when present. Purely a record; no constraints live here, they're posted in build.

services/api/horolog/solver/model.py::Bu.oneLiner: CpModel plus the var index and warm-start hints
services/api/horolog/solver/model.py::Bu.detail: chunks maps (requirement_index, chunk_index) -> ChunkVars so the caller can read the solution back after solving; hints holds (var, value) pairs already applied to the model. requirements is kept in the same order the indices refer to — don't reorder it.

services/api/horolog/solver/model.py::bu.oneLiner: Builds the CP-SAT scheduling model from requirements
services/api/horolog/solver/model.py::bu.detail: Takes requirements, busy intervals, horizon length, and optional prior schedule/weights/warm-start hint; returns a BuiltModel wrapping the CpModel, per-chunk vars, and hint pairs. Each requirement becomes n_chunks optional intervals with size 0 or ≥min_chunk, one window literal chosen via AddExactlyOne, chunks forced in order and filled front-to-back via AddImplication; busy events and locked blocks are fixed intervals in the same NoOverlap, so no intent can displace them. Objective mixes priority-weighted placement reward against penalties for fragmentation, lateness past due_slot, deviation from preferred_offset, and movement from the previous schedule capped at perturb_cap.

services/api/horolog/solver/solve.py::so.oneLiner: Schedules intent demand around busy slots, returns Plan
services/api/horolog/solver/solve.py::so.detail: Expands intents into per-occurrence requirements, merges busy intervals, and calls `construct` to place chunks, biasing toward `previous` placements so blocks stay put. Raises ValueError only for horizon_slots <= 0; over-subscribed calendars yield partial placement plus UnmetDemand entries, blocks sorted by (start_slot, intent_id), and solve_ms wall-clock timing on the Plan.

services/api/horolog/solver/solve.py::_s.oneLiner: Wraps a requirement plus placed count as UnmetDemand
services/api/horolog/solver/solve.py::_s.detail: Pure record constructor copying intent_id, occurrence, required_slots and priority off the Requirement. Called with placed=0 for the whole-model-failed path and with the actual placed slot count for partial placements.

services/api/horolog/solver/solve.py::me.oneLiner: Collapses overlapping busy intervals into disjoint ones
services/api/horolog/solver/solve.py::me.detail: Sorts by (start_slot, end_slot) and merges any interval starting at or before the previous end, concatenating source_id and label with '+'; returns [] for empty input. Works on model_copy so callers' objects are untouched, but an interval fully contained in the previous one is dropped silently — its source_id and label never appear in the output. Touching intervals (start == end) merge, so the result is disjoint and non-adjacent.

services/api/tests/test_solver.py::at.oneLiner: Converts (day, hour) to an absolute slot index
services/api/tests/test_solver.py::at.detail: Multiplies day by SLOTS_PER_DAY and hour by SLOTS_PER_HOUR, sums them. Test-local coordinate helper for writing readable slot literals.

services/api/tests/test_solver.py::workd.detail: Takes start/end in hours, returns a one-element list of DailyWindow with minute offsets. Default availability for tasks that don't care about windows.

services/api/tests/test_solver.py::task.oneLiner: Factory for a TASK Intent with sane defaults
services/api/tests/test_solver.py::task.detail: Returns Intent(kind=TASK) with id/title equal to ident, 120 min, P3, 60–120 min chunks, workday windows. Body references a `kw` dict and `due_slot` used at call sites that aren't in the shown signature — signature is out of sync with usage.

services/api/tests/test_solver.py::asser.oneLiner: Asserts plan invariants: no overlap, in horizon, off busy
services/api/tests/test_solver.py::asser.detail: Sorts blocks by start_slot, checks adjacent pairs don't overlap, each block has positive length within horizon_slots, and no block intersects any BusyInterval. Raises AssertionError with the offending block; returns nothing.

services/api/tests/test_solver.py::test_.oneLiner: Empty week: a 120-min task gets scheduled in full
services/api/tests/test_solver.py::test_.detail: Solves one 120-minute intent against no busy intervals over WEEK, then asserts soundness, that block slots sum to minutes_to_slots(120), and that unmet is empty. Baseline happy path — total scheduled duration is checked as a slot sum across blocks, so splitting into multiple blocks is allowed.

services/api/tests/test_solver.py::test_.oneLiner: Asserts scheduled blocks never span a window gap
services/api/tests/test_solver.py::test_.detail: Builds a 9–12 / 13–17 split-day availability, asks the solver for one unsplittable 180-minute task, and checks every returned block falls entirely in the morning or entirely in the afternoon range. Relies on module helpers `task`, `solve`, `at`, and `SLOTS_PER_DAY`; `block.start_slot // SLOTS_PER_DAY` recovers the day index so `at(day, hour)` yields an absolute slot for comparison. Also asserts `plan.blocks` is non-empty, so a solver that schedules nothing fails rather than passing vacuously.

services/api/tests/test_solver.py::test_.oneLiner: Busy time is hard: even P1 yields and reports shortfall
services/api/tests/test_solver.py::test_.detail: Fills 9–17 every day for 7 days with busy intervals, then solves a P1 120-min task. Expects zero blocks and unmet[0].shortfall_slots equal to the full request.

services/api/tests/test_solver.py::test_.oneLiner: P1 beats P4 for the single available hour
services/api/tests/test_solver.py::test_.detail: Two 60-min fixed-chunk intents share one 10–11 window over a single day. Expects only "critical" scheduled and "trivial" listed as the sole unmet intent.

services/api/tests/test_solver.py::test_.oneLiner: Re-solve with previous plan perturbs only the hit day
services/api/tests/test_solver.py::test_.detail: Solves five tasks, adds an all-day busy interval on day 5, re-solves with previous=first. Asserts perturbation_slots stays within displaced slots plus one day's slack, and that all but one non-displaced block keeps start_slot == moved_from.

services/api/tests/test_solver.py::test_.oneLiner: Impossible demand yields unmet entries, not an exception
services/api/tests/test_solver.py::test_.detail: Builds 20 P3 intents of 480 minutes each (160 hours, far past a week), solves with no busy intervals, and asserts the plan is still sound and plan.unmet is non-empty. Pins the contract that the solver degrades gracefully instead of raising or returning an infeasible plan.

services/api/tests/test_solver.py::test_.oneLiner: Weekly habit yields one occurrence per week, max 1/day
services/api/tests/test_solver.py::test_.detail: A 180-min/7-day habit with 60-min chunks and max_per_day=1 over three weeks. Asserts occurrence ids are exactly {0,1,2} and each occurrence's blocks land on distinct days.

services/api/tests/test_solver.py::test_.oneLiner: All blocks land before the intent's due_slot
services/api/tests/test_solver.py::test_.detail: Task due at day 1, 17:00 over a week horizon. Asserts blocks exist and max end_slot is at or before the due slot.

services/api/tests/test_solver.py::test_.oneLiner: merge_busy coalesces overlapping intervals, keeps gaps
services/api/tests/test_solver.py::test_.detail: Feeds 10–20, 15–30, 40–50 from different sources. Expects [(10,30),(40,50)] — overlaps unioned across sources, disjoint span preserved.

services/api/tests/test_solver.py::test_.oneLiner: Overlapping busy intervals don't break the solver
services/api/tests/test_solver.py::test_.detail: Feeds two overlapping BusyInterval rows (day 0 09:00–12:00 and 10:00–14:00) plus one 60-min task and asserts the plan is sound against that busy list. Guards against the solver assuming busy intervals are disjoint or pre-merged; only soundness is checked, not placement.

services/api/tests/test_solver.py::test_.oneLiner: expand drops partial trailing period of a habit
services/api/tests/test_solver.py::test_.detail: Weekly habit expanded over 10 days (WEEK + 3 days) yields exactly one occurrence. Prevents a partial week from counting as permanent shortfall.

services/api/tests/test_solver.py::test_.oneLiner: Window shorter than min_chunk raises ValueError at build
services/api/tests/test_solver.py::test_.detail: A 120-min min_chunk against a 30-minute window. Expects pytest.raises(ValueError) matching "shorter than min_chunk" — validation fires in Intent construction, before solve.

services/api/dbg.py::task.oneLiner: Builds a P3 Intent test fixture from an id string
services/api/dbg.py::task.detail: Takes `i`, used as both id and title; returns an Intent of kind TASK needing 120 min per period, chunked 60–120 min, schedulable only in a 9:00–17:00 window. Test/demo helper — window minutes are offsets from midnight, and every field but the id is hardcoded.

services/api/tests/test_solver.py::test_.oneLiner: Asserts scheduler keeps non-colliding blocks in place
services/api/tests/test_solver.py::test_.detail: Solves 5 P3 tasks over WEEK, re-solves with a day-5 09:00-17:00 BusyInterval passed as `previous=first`, then checks every block from the first solution that does not overlap the interval still exists in the second at the identical start_slot. Overlap uses half-open comparison (start < intrusion.end and intrusion.start < end); the check is per-block, not aggregate travel distance, so a single untouched block drifting fails even if total movement is small.

services/api/tests/test_solver.py::test_.oneLiner: Re-solving identical input keeps every block in place
services/api/tests/test_solver.py::test_.detail: Solves 5 P3 tasks of 120 min against one busy standup interval, then re-solves passing the first schedule as `previous`. Asserts `perturbation_slots == 0` and that the key→start_slot map is identical, so the solver is idempotent to the slot.

services/api/tests/test_solver.py::test_.oneLiner: New meeting moves only colliding blocks, plus at most one
services/api/tests/test_solver.py::test_.detail: Solves 5 tasks with no busy time, injects a day-5 9-17 offsite, re-solves with `previous=first`, and checks soundness. Counts blocks overlapping the intrusion (`displaced`) and blocks whose start moved (`moved`); requires no block dropped and `moved <= displaced + 1` — the +1 is the allowed knock-on from re-packing that day, so perturbation is bounded in aggregate, not per block.

services/api/horolog/bench.py::_populati.detail: Seeded `random.Random(seed)` makes output deterministic; cycles kinds TASK/HABIT/FOCUS by index, weights recurring kinds 3x vs TASK 1x, and splits UTILISATION of total capacity across that weight so the set roughly fills the horizon. Per-intent minutes are jittered 0.6–1.4x and rounded to 30-min steps with a 30-min floor, so the actual total drifts from the budget; TASK gets `period_days=None` (one-shot), others 7.

services/api/horolog/bench.py::_meetings.oneLiner: Synthetic busy calendar: 1-4 meetings/day over 21 days
services/api/horolog/bench.py::_meetings.detail: Seeded RNG (seed+1, so meeting layout decorrelates from _population's seed) emits BusyIntervals starting on hour boundaries 09:00-16:00, each exactly 2 slots long. Intervals may overlap or duplicate — callers that care must run merge_busy first, as the quality loop does but the timing loop does not.

services/api/horolog/bench.py::run.oneLiner: Benchmarks solve() cold vs warm-start over REPEATS seeds
services/api/horolog/bench.py::run.detail: For each seed it builds a synthetic intent population and busy set, solves once (cold), then re-solves with one extra 8-slot BusyInterval injected on day 5 while passing the prior Plan as `previous` (warm). Returns cold ms list, warm ms list, objective scores from CP-SAT runs only, count of CP-SAT runs, and the last cold Plan — so the returned Plan is seed REPEATS-1's, not a representative one; `scores` is shorter than `cold` whenever a fallback engine ran.

services/api/horolog/bench.py::main.oneLiner: Prints scaling benchmark table plus quality scores
services/api/horolog/bench.py::main.detail: For 30/100/300 intents runs REPEATS seeds: cold solve, then a warm re-solve with one extra 8-slot busy block injected on day 5, recording solve_ms for both and perturbation_slots as churn; prints median/p95 plus load (demand/_capacity_slots) and block/unmet counts. Gotcha: blocks and unmet come from the last seed's plan while reqs/demand are recomputed at seed 0, so those columns describe different populations; second loop reports score() on a fresh construct() with merged busy.

services/api/horolog/solver/greedy.py::_.oneLiner: Sorted busy-interval set with earliest-free-gap lookup
services/api/horolog/solver/greedy.py::_.detail: Wraps a list of [start, end) slot spans kept sorted by start; answers whether a run of N slots is free and where the earliest such run begins. Mutable — take() records new occupancy in place. Spans are never merged, so overlapping/adjacent entries accumulate.

services/api/horolog/solver/greedy.py::_.oneLiner: Sorts BusyInterval objects into (start, end) tuples
services/api/horolog/solver/greedy.py::_.detail: Takes busy intervals, stores them as tuples sorted by start then end in self._spans. Copies, so the caller's list is untouched.

services/api/horolog/solver/greedy.py::_.oneLiner: True if [start, start+size) is clear and fits in [lo, hi)
services/api/horolog/solver/greedy.py::_.detail: Checks the exact placement at lo, not any placement in the range: returns False if no span overlaps [lo, lo+size) and the window is wide enough. Scans every span — O(n), no early exit despite the sort.

services/api/horolog/solver/greedy.py::_.oneLiner: Earliest start in [lo, hi) with `size` free slots
services/api/horolog/solver/greedy.py::_.detail: Walks spans in sorted order, pushing a cursor past each one that blocks it, and stops early once a gap of `size` opens before the next span. Returns None if the window is too narrow or the cursor runs past hi; correctness depends on _spans being sorted by start.
insort keeps _spans sorted, so subsequent first_fit calls stay valid. No overlap check — booking an already-busy range silently duplicates coverage.

services/api/horolog/solver/greedy.py::c.oneLiner: Splits required slots into ≤limit chunks, largest first
services/api/horolog/solver/greedy.py::c.detail: Greedily takes max_chunk at a time, but shaves a chunk when the leftover would fall below min_chunk, so no undersized tail is emitted. Stops at `limit` chunks or when the remainder drops under min_chunk — the returned sizes can sum to less than `required`.

services/api/horolog/solver/greedy.py::_.oneLiner: Ranks a requirement's windows, best candidate first
services/api/horolog/solver/greedy.py::_.detail: Three tiers: a window containing this chunk's previous start slot, then windows whose lo is nearest the preferred time of day, then earliest lo. Returns indices into req.windows, keyed by (intent_id, occurrence, chunk) in `previous`; ties break on window.lo.

services/api/horolog/solver/greedy.py::c.oneLiner: Greedy first-fit placement of requirement chunks
services/api/horolog/solver/greedy.py::c.detail: Sorts requirements by (priority, kind rank, due_slot, intent_id), splits each into chunks via chunk_sizes, and takes the first free slot range in each candidate window, preferring the chunk's start_slot from `previous` when it still fits (schedule stability). Returns a Placement mapping (requirement index, chunk) -> (start, size); unfittable chunks are silently dropped, max_per_day caps chunks per day, and the _Occupancy is local so `busy` is not mutated.

services/api/horolog/solver/solve.py::_p.oneLiner: Converts a greedy placement into a FEASIBLE Plan.
services/api/horolog/solver/solve.py::_p.detail: Fallback path when CP-SAT returns no usable status: reads (start, size) tuples out of the Placement dict keyed by (requirement index, chunk), emits ScheduledBlocks sorted by (start_slot, intent_id), and records shortfalls in unmet. Status is hardcoded FEASIBLE and engine GREEDY with no objective value, so callers comparing objectives across runs must handle its absence.

services/api/horolog/bench.py::_capacity.oneLiner: Total schedulable slots across a 3-week horizon
services/api/horolog/bench.py::_capacity.detail: Multiplies 21 days by waking hours (DAY_END_H - DAY_START_H) times SLOTS_PER_HOUR. Pure, no args; assumes every day has an identical window and ignores existing commitments.

services/api/horolog/bench.py::_p95.detail: Uses statistics.quantiles(n=100)[94]; falls back to values[0] for a single sample. Raises IndexError on an empty list, and with few samples the cut point is interpolated, not an observed value.

services/api/horolog/domain/plan.py::Eng.oneLiner: StrEnum naming which solver produced a plan
services/api/horolog/domain/plan.py::Eng.detail: Two members: CP_SAT ("cp-sat") and GREEDY ("greedy"). GREEDY means the construction heuristic's output survived because CP-SAT found nothing better in its time budget — feasible but unoptimized; persistent GREEDY signals under-provisioned solve time or an over-subscribed problem.

services/api/qual.py::score.oneLiner: Scores a placement using the solver's objective function
services/api/qual.py::score.detail: Sums per-chunk value over placed chunks: (W.place[priority] - W.kind_tiebreak*KIND_RANK[kind]) * size, minus W.fragment per placed chunk. Unplaced chunks (missing (ri,k) key) contribute nothing; the second element of the placement tuple is the size, the first (a machine/bin id) is ignored. Pure, no side effects — use it to verify a solver result matches its reported objective.

hard.py::score.oneLiner: Sums weighted placement value minus fragment penalty
hard.py::score.detail: Iterates every (requirement index, chunk index) pair, looks it up in `place` dict; missing/falsy entries are skipped. Each hit adds `(W.place[priority] - W.kind_tiebreak * KIND_RANK[kind]) * f[1]` and subtracts a flat `W.fragment`, so `f[1]` is the chunk's slot count/duration and every extra chunk costs a fixed amount.

hard.py::hard.oneLiner: Generates n seeded random Intents as a stress fixture
hard.py::hard.detail: Deterministic via `random.Random(seed)`; picks a random IntentKind, remapping BUFFER→TASK, and gives each intent two daily windows (morning 8–11ish, afternoon 13–15ish) plus random priority 1–4 and 30/60/90 minutes per period. Gotchas: `period_days=7` only for HABIT/FOCUS, `due_slot` only for TASK, `max_per_day` is 1 or None by coin flip, and `max_chunk_minutes == minutes_per_period` so a whole period can land in one chunk.

hard.py::meetings.oneLiner: Generates seeded random BusyIntervals over a 14-day span
hard.py::meetings.detail: For each of 14 days emits 3–7 intervals starting at a random hour 8–16, length 2 or 4 slots, seeded with `seed+99` so it varies independently of `hard(seed)`. Intervals may overlap or duplicate — no collision check — and `source_id` reuses the loop var `_` as an index.

services/api/hard.py::score.oneLiner: Sums weighted objective value of a chunk placement
services/api/hard.py::score.detail: Walks every (requirement index, chunk index) pair, looks it up in `place` dict; missing/falsy entries are skipped. Each placed chunk adds `(W.place[priority] - W.kind_tiebreak * KIND_RANK[kind]) * f[1] - W.fragment`, where `f[1]` is presumably the chunk's slot count — so unplaced chunks contribute 0 and every placed chunk pays a fixed fragmentation penalty.

services/api/hard.py::hard.oneLiner: Generates n synthetic stress-test Intents from a seed
services/api/hard.py::hard.detail: Deterministic via `random.Random(seed)`; returns a list of `Intent` with ids/titles `h0..h{n-1}`, random kind/priority, two daily windows (a morning one at a–b, an afternoon one at c–d), and 30-min minimum chunks. Kind-conditional fields: `period_days=7` only for HABIT/FOCUS, `due_slot` only for TASK; `max_per_day` is 1 or None on a coin flip, and `preferred_start_min` may fall outside neither window since it's drawn from {None, a*60, c*60}.

services/api/hard.py::meetings.oneLiner: Generates random busy intervals over a 14-day horizon
services/api/hard.py::meetings.detail: Uses `random.Random(seed + 99)` so it stays independent of `hard(seed)`; emits 3–7 `BusyInterval`s per day starting on the hour between 08:00 and 16:00, each 2 or 4 slots long. Intervals may overlap or duplicate — the (day, hour, j) id scheme keeps them unique but doesn't prevent collisions, and 4-slot blocks at hour 16 can run past the intended end of day.

services/api/horolog/solver/score.py::We.oneLiner: Scoring coefficients with self-enforcing sanity checks
services/api/horolog/solver/score.py::We.detail: Pydantic model holding per-priority placement rewards, kind tiebreak, fragmentation penalty, and perturbation penalty plus its cap. Defaults encode preemption (P1 is 10x P4), and the validator rejects any override where a penalty could outweigh scheduling work at all.

services/api/horolog/solver/score.py::We.oneLiner: Post-init validator rejecting weight sets that invert priorities
services/api/horolog/solver/score.py::We.detail: Checks three things: cheapest place weight exceeds fragment (so placing beats dropping), kind_tiebreak times max KIND_RANK stays under the smallest gap between priority tiers (so kind never outranks priority), and perturb times perturb_cap stays under the reward for a minimum-sane-size block (so stability never outranks scheduling). Raises ValueError with the offending numbers; returns self.

services/api/horolog/solver/score.py::sc.oneLiner: Total score of a placement: reward minus churn and splits
services/api/horolog/solver/score.py::sc.detail: For each requirement's chunks, adds (priority weight minus kind_tiebreak * KIND_RANK) * slot count, subtracts one fragment penalty per placed chunk, and subtracts perturb * capped slot distance from that chunk's previous start. Unplaced chunks score zero; placement is keyed by requirement index while previous_starts is keyed by (intent_id, occurrence, chunk), so a re-ordered requirements list still matches history. Pure, no side effects.

services/api/horolog/domain/plan.py::Pla.oneLiner: True when nothing was left unplaced
services/api/horolog/domain/plan.py::Pla.detail: Property returning `not self.unmet`. Says every demand was placed, not that the placement is good — quality lives in `perturbation_slots`.

services/api/tests/test_solver.py::test_.oneLiner: Seeded fuzz: 60 random intents on a crowded calendar
services/api/tests/test_solver.py::test_.detail: Builds 60 intents (seed 7) with split daily windows, 30/60/90-min chunks, optional max_per_day and due_slot, plus 4 random 1-hour busy blocks per day over 14 days, then calls solve over a 2-week horizon and runs assert_sound against the merged busy list, requiring at least one placed block. Re-solves with previous=plan and asserts perturbation_slots == 0, so the heuristic must be stable; the seed makes it deterministic, and changing the generation logic or the heuristics can flip it without any real regression.

services/api/horolog/settings.py::Settin.oneLiner: Pydantic BaseSettings holding all app config
services/api/horolog/settings.py::Settin.detail: Reads HOROLOG_-prefixed env vars and .env, ignoring unknown keys; every field has a working default so it constructs bare. Validators reject unknown timezones and inverted workday bounds at instantiation, so a bad env fails at startup, not at request time.

services/api/horolog/settings.py::Settin.oneLiner: Rejects timezone strings the IANA db lacks
services/api/horolog/settings.py::Settin.detail: field_validator on timezone: builds a ZoneInfo and re-raises ZoneInfoNotFoundError as ValueError, otherwise returns the string unchanged. Depends on the host tzdata (or the tzdata package on systems without one), so the same value can pass locally and fail in a slim container.

field_validator on workday_end_min reads the already-validated workday_start_min from info.data and raises ValueError if end is not strictly greater. Skips the check when start is absent — i.e. when start itself failed validation — and relies on field declaration order, so moving workday_end_min above workday_start_min silently disables it.

services/api/horolog/settings.py::Settin.oneLiner: timezone string as a ZoneInfo object
services/api/horolog/settings.py::Settin.detail: Property returning ZoneInfo(self.timezone) for date math; safe because the validator already proved the name resolves. Constructs on every access, though ZoneInfo caches instances internally.

services/api/horolog/settings.py::settin.detail: Zero-arg factory used as a FastAPI dependency / accessor so env is read through one place. As written it builds a fresh Settings on every call — no caching, no singleton — so add @lru_cache if repeated construction or re-reading .env matters.

services/api/horolog/db.py::Base.oneLiner: SQLAlchemy 2.0 declarative base for all tables
services/api/horolog/db.py::Base.detail: Empty subclass of DeclarativeBase; carries the shared MetaData that IntentRow, BusyRow and PlanRow register into. init_db reads Base.metadata to emit DDL.

services/api/horolog/db.py::IntentRow.oneLiner: Table `intents`: whole Intent stored as one JSON blob
services/api/horolog/db.py::IntentRow.detail: String(64) id, `payload` JSON column holding the full validated Intent, `created_at` defaulting to UTC now at insert. No shredded columns, so you cannot filter or index on Intent fields in SQL — query in Python after load_intents.

services/api/horolog/db.py::IntentRow.to.oneLiner: Rehydrate the JSON payload into an Intent
services/api/horolog/db.py::IntentRow.to.detail: Runs Intent.model_validate on the stored dict, returning the Pydantic model. Raises ValidationError if the row predates a schema change — there is no migration path for old payloads.

services/api/horolog/db.py::BusyRow.detail: String(128) id, `source` in {manual, caldav, google}, free-text `label`, and integer `start_slot`/`end_slot` (slot indices, not timestamps). Only start_slot is indexed, so range scans filter on it first.

services/api/horolog/db.py::PlanRow.oneLiner: Table `plans`: a Plan serialized as JSON text
services/api/horolog/db.py::PlanRow.detail: Integer primary key, `payload` Text holding model_dump_json output, `saved_at` UTC. Column is Text not JSON, so the DB cannot introspect it; only LATEST_PLAN_ID is ever written.

services/api/horolog/db.py::init_db.oneLiner: Create any missing tables on the engine
services/api/horolog/db.py::init_db.detail: Opens a transaction on the module-level `_engine` and runs create_all in a thread via run_sync. Creates missing tables only — never alters existing ones, so schema changes need a manual migration or a wiped DB.

services/api/horolog/db.py::session.detail: Built for FastAPI's Depends; the `async with` closes the session after the request. Does not commit or roll back — callers commit themselves (see save_plan).

services/api/horolog/db.py::load_intents.oneLiner: Load every intents row as domain Intent objects
services/api/horolog/db.py::load_intents.detail: Unfiltered SELECT over the whole table, then to_domain on each row. No pagination or ordering; cost grows with table size and one bad payload fails the entire call.

services/api/horolog/db.py::load_previou.oneLiner: Fetch the single saved Plan, or None
services/api/horolog/db.py::load_previou.detail: Primary-key get on LATEST_PLAN_ID, then json.loads plus Plan.model_validate. Returns None when nothing has been saved yet; raises on a payload that no longer matches the Plan schema.

services/api/horolog/db.py::save_plan.oneLiner: Upsert the Plan at LATEST_PLAN_ID and commit
services/api/horolog/db.py::save_plan.detail: Inserts a new PlanRow if absent, otherwise overwrites payload and bumps saved_at, then commits. Only one plan row exists — every save destroys the previous plan, and this is the only function here that commits.

services/api/horolog/api.py::origin.oneLiner: Midnight today in the configured timezone
services/api/horolog/api.py::origin.detail: Returns today's 00:00:00 in settings().zone, computed fresh on every call so a long-lived process rolls over at midnight. Serves as the slot-index base for every datetime↔slot conversion.

services/api/horolog/api.py::horizon_slo.detail: horizon_days × SLOTS_PER_DAY. Passed to solve() as the upper bound on schedulable slot indices.

services/api/horolog/api.py::IntentIn.oneLiner: Wire model for a thing to schedule
services/api/horolog/api.py::IntentIn.detail: Validates bounds at the boundary (title 1-200 chars, positive minutes/chunks/period) and defaults kind=TASK, priority=P3, chunks 30-120 min. `to_domain(ident, base)` builds the `Intent`: unset window_start_min/window_end_min fall back to the configured workday, and earliest/due convert to slot indices relative to `base`.

services/api/horolog/api.py::IntentIn.to.oneLiner: Convert request body to domain Intent
services/api/horolog/api.py::IntentIn.to.detail: Fills unset window bounds from settings().workday_start_min/end_min, wraps them in a single DailyWindow, and converts earliest/due datetimes to slot indices relative to base. Raises ValueError on domain validation failure; the caller turns that into a 422.

services/api/horolog/api.py::BusyIn.oneLiner: Wire model for a blocked-off interval
services/api/horolog/api.py::BusyIn.detail: Carries label, start, end, and a `source` tag defaulting to "manual". Start/end go through `_localise`; `source` is what `_mirror` scopes its deletes to, so manual entries survive a calendar sync.

services/api/horolog/api.py::BlockOut.oneLiner: One scheduled block with real datetimes
services/api/horolog/api.py::BlockOut.detail: API view of a solver block: slot indices already converted back to datetimes, plus intent title and kind denormalized in. moved_from is non-null when the replan shifted this block off its previous position.

services/api/horolog/api.py::UnmetOut.oneLiner: Intent the solver could not fully place
services/api/horolog/api.py::UnmetOut.detail: Reports shortfall in minutes (solver slots × 15). Presence here means the plan is partial even if solve succeeded.

services/api/horolog/api.py::PlanOut.oneLiner: Full plan response: blocks, gaps, busy, timings
services/api/horolog/api.py::PlanOut.detail: Bundles the schedule with the busy mirror and solver metadata (solve_ms, complete). origin and horizon_days let a client anchor and bound the rendered timeline.

services/api/horolog/api.py::Broadcast.oneLiner: In-process fan-out of plan events to SSE clients
services/api/horolog/api.py::Broadcast.detail: Holds a set of bounded queues, one per connected client. Single-process only — with multiple workers, a publish on one worker never reaches clients on another.

services/api/horolog/api.py::Broadcast._.oneLiner: Start with an empty subscriber set
services/api/horolog/api.py::Broadcast._.detail: Creates the set of per-client asyncio queues. No I/O, safe to construct at import time.

services/api/horolog/api.py::Broadcast.s.oneLiner: Async context manager yielding a client queue
services/api/horolog/api.py::Broadcast.s.detail: Registers a queue with maxsize=16 and removes it on exit, including on exception or client disconnect. Yields the queue for the caller to await on.

services/api/horolog/api.py::Broadcast.p.oneLiner: Push an event to every subscriber, dropping if full
services/api/horolog/api.py::Broadcast.p.detail: Iterates a copy of the subscriber set so concurrent subscribe/unsubscribe is safe, and uses put_nowait with QueueFull suppressed. A slow client silently loses events rather than blocking the publisher.

services/api/horolog/api.py::lifespan.oneLiner: FastAPI startup hook that initializes the database
services/api/horolog/api.py::lifespan.detail: Awaits init_db() before serving, then yields for the app's lifetime. No shutdown work.

services/api/horolog/api.py::health.detail: Touches no database or solver. Success means the process is up, not that dependencies are.

services/api/horolog/api.py::list_intent.oneLiner: Return all stored intents as raw JSON payloads
services/api/horolog/api.py::list_intent.detail: Selects every IntentRow and returns row.payload directly, bypassing Pydantic re-validation. Unpaginated.

services/api/horolog/api.py::create_inte.oneLiner: Persist a new intent and replan
services/api/horolog/api.py::create_inte.detail: Generates a 12-hex-char id, converts the body to a domain Intent (ValueError → 422), stores it as JSON, commits, then triggers _replan which saves a new plan and publishes an SSE event. Returns the domain intent, not the stored row.

services/api/horolog/api.py::delete_inte.oneLiner: Delete an intent by id and replan
services/api/horolog/api.py::delete_inte.detail: 404s when the row is missing. On success commits the delete then runs _replan, so the freed time is immediately reallocated.

services/api/horolog/api.py::replace_bus.oneLiner: Replace the whole busy mirror, then replan
services/api/horolog/api.py::replace_bus.detail: Deletes all BusyRow and reinserts the posted events as slot ranges relative to origin(); rejects any event with end <= start as 422. Wholesale replacement means a deleted upstream meeting actually frees its slot. Returns event and block counts.

services/api/horolog/api.py::get_plan.oneLiner: Return the saved plan, solving only if none exists
services/api/horolog/api.py::get_plan.detail: Loads the persisted plan and falls back to _replan when the store is empty. Read-mostly — an existing plan is returned unchanged, so it can be stale relative to edits made outside the API.

services/api/horolog/api.py::resolve.oneLiner: Force a fresh solve and return the new plan
services/api/horolog/api.py::resolve.detail: Always runs _replan, persisting the result and publishing an SSE event, then renders it. Use when the caller wants recomputation rather than the cached plan.

services/api/horolog/api.py::stream.detail: Subscribes to the broadcast bus and emits a "plan" event per published payload, with a "ping" event every 20s of silence to keep the connection alive. The payload carries only block count and solve_ms — clients must refetch the plan.

services/api/horolog/api.py::_replan.oneLiner: Solve, persist, and announce a new plan
services/api/horolog/api.py::_replan.detail: Loads intents and busy rows, calls solve() with the horizon and the previous plan (for move minimization), saves the result, and publishes a summary on the bus. Every mutating endpoint routes through it.

services/api/horolog/api.py::_render.oneLiner: Convert a domain Plan into the API PlanOut
services/api/horolog/api.py::_render.detail: Maps slot indices back to datetimes via origin() and joins each block to its intent for title and kind, falling back to the raw intent_id and IntentKind.TASK when the intent is gone. Unmet shortfall is converted from slots to minutes by ×15, hardcoding the 15-minute slot size.

services/api/tests/test_api.py::client.oneLiner: Pytest fixture: async HTTP client on the ASGI app
services/api/tests/test_api.py::client.detail: Runs init_db(), wires AsyncClient through ASGITransport (no network), then wipes state by deleting every existing intent and PUTting an empty busy list. Yields the client; shared DB means isolation depends on that manual cleanup, not rollback.

services/api/tests/test_api.py::test_hea.detail: Smoke test that the app boots and routes. No state touched.

services/api/tests/test_api.py::test_cre.oneLiner: New intent is placed on the plan right away
services/api/tests/test_api.py::test_cre.detail: POSTs one 120-min intent, asserts 201, then GETs /api/plan and requires at least one block with that title, complete is True, and solve_ms under 500. Couples correctness to a wall-clock latency budget, so it can flake on a slow machine.

services/api/tests/test_api.py::test_bus.oneLiner: Busy events move blocks and never overlap them
services/api/tests/test_api.py::test_bus.detail: Schedules a rigid 120-min block, records its start, PUTs three days of 09:00–17:00 busy windows anchored at origin(), re-reads the plan. Asserts the block moved and that no block overlaps the first busy window (overlap check covers only blocked[0]).

services/api/tests/test_api.py::test_rep.oneLiner: Re-solving an unchanged calendar is stable
services/api/tests/test_api.py::test_rep.detail: Creates 4 intents, POSTs /api/plan/solve twice, compares a dict keyed by intent_id:occurrence:chunk to start time. Catches solver nondeterminism and gratuitous churn; ignores block order and any field other than start.

services/api/tests/test_api.py::test_imp.detail: POSTs a 240-min min_chunk into a 30-minute window (600–630) and expects 422 with "min_chunk" in detail. Asserts validation happens at create time, not silently at solve time.

services/api/tests/test_api.py::test_ove.oneLiner: Excess demand is reported as unmet, not dropped
services/api/tests/test_api.py::test_ove.detail: Creates 40 intents of 480 min each, then requires plan complete False, non-empty unmet, and first entry shortfall_minutes > 0. Slow-ish: 40 sequential POSTs each likely triggering a re-solve.

services/api/horolog/llm.py::ExtractionF.oneLiner: Raised when the model can't yield a valid object
services/api/horolog/llm.py::ExtractionF.detail: Subclasses RuntimeError. Thrown after the repair round fails, on non-JSON output, or on an Anthropic refusal — catch it to fall back to a manual form.

services/api/horolog/llm.py::strict_sche.oneLiner: Pydantic schema rewritten for constrained decoding
services/api/horolog/llm.py::strict_sche.detail: Takes a BaseModel subclass, returns its JSON Schema mutated in place: every object gets `additionalProperties: false` and all properties marked required, and numeric/length/format keywords are stripped since neither engine accepts them. Those dropped bounds still apply at `model_validate_json` time, so optional fields must be typed `X | None` or the model is forced to invent a value.

services/api/horolog/llm.py::Provider.oneLiner: Protocol for anything that returns schema-shaped JSON
services/api/horolog/llm.py::Provider.detail: Structural typing — no base class to inherit. Two implementations here: OpenAICompatible and AnthropicProvider.

services/api/horolog/llm.py::Provider.co.oneLiner: Protocol method: prompt in, JSON string out
services/api/horolog/llm.py::Provider.co.detail: Args: system prompt, user prompt, JSON Schema dict, schema name for the provider's grammar label. Returns a raw JSON string; parsing and validation happen in `extract`.

services/api/horolog/llm.py::OpenAICompa.detail: Covers Ollama, vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, OpenAI. Deliberately no `openai` SDK dependency for a single POST.

services/api/horolog/llm.py::OpenAICompa.oneLiner: Stores endpoint URL, model, key, timeout
services/api/horolog/llm.py::OpenAICompa.detail: Appends `/chat/completions` to `base_url` after stripping a trailing slash — pass the API root, not the full endpoint. No client is created here; each call opens its own.

services/api/horolog/llm.py::OpenAICompa.oneLiner: POSTs one chat completion, returns message content
services/api/horolog/llm.py::OpenAICompa.detail: Sends `response_format.json_schema` with `strict: true` and `temperature: 0`; raises `httpx.HTTPStatusError` on non-2xx and KeyError if the response shape differs. A fresh `AsyncClient` per call means no connection pooling across requests.

services/api/horolog/llm.py::AnthropicPr.oneLiner: Claude via the official async SDK
services/api/horolog/llm.py::AnthropicPr.detail: Separate from the OpenAI path because Anthropic uses `output_config.format`, not `response_format`. Requires the optional `horolog[anthropic]` extra.

services/api/horolog/llm.py::AnthropicPr.oneLiner: Imports the SDK lazily, builds AsyncAnthropic
services/api/horolog/llm.py::AnthropicPr.detail: Missing package raises RuntimeError with the install command instead of ImportError at module load. Empty `api_key` becomes None, letting the SDK read `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from the environment.

services/api/horolog/llm.py::AnthropicPr.oneLiner: One messages.create call, text blocks concatenated
services/api/horolog/llm.py::AnthropicPr.detail: Caps output at 2048 tokens and passes the schema via `output_config`; `stop_reason == "refusal"` raises ExtractionFailed. Non-text blocks are dropped, and a `max_tokens` truncation yields silently invalid JSON that only surfaces as a parse error upstream.

services/api/horolog/llm.py::build_provi.detail: Anthropic when `llm_provider == "anthropic"`, OpenAICompatible otherwise. Reads config on every call and constructs a new client.

services/api/horolog/llm.py::extract.oneLiner: Text to validated Pydantic model, one repair retry
services/api/horolog/llm.py::extract.detail: Calls the provider with `strict_schema(schema_model)`, validates the JSON; on ValidationError it resends the user prompt plus the error text and validates once more. Second failure or non-JSON raises ExtractionFailed — so a bad extraction costs up to two round trips, and `provider` defaults to `build_provider()` unless injected.

services/api/horolog/capture.py::IntentD.oneLiner: LLM output schema for a scheduling intent, human units
services/api/horolog/capture.py::IntentD.detail: Fields are minutes, days, and times-per-period instead of the engine's 15-minute slots, so the model never does the conversion arithmetic. Pydantic validates on construction; `_sane` runs after field parsing and raises ValueError on incoherent combinations.

services/api/horolog/capture.py::IntentD.oneLiner: Post-init validator rejecting incoherent draft fields
services/api/horolog/capture.py::IntentD.detail: Enforces positive durations, min_chunk <= max_chunk, at least one chunk fitting both minutes_per_period and the daily window, window bounds set as a pair inside 0..1440, and non-negative due_in_days. Returns self or raises ValueError with a message naming the fix.

services/api/horolog/capture.py::to_payl.oneLiner: Builds the POST /api/intents body from a draft
services/api/horolog/capture.py::to_payl.detail: Rounds minutes_per_period and both chunk bounds up to the 15-minute grid — rounding down would schedule a 20-minute task for 15 and mark it complete — while window bounds, period_days, and max_per_day pass through unchanged. Adds `due` as an ISO timestamp of `now + due_in_days` only when due_in_days is set; `now` is caller-supplied, so no clock is read here.

services/api/horolog/capture.py::capture.oneLiner: Extracts an IntentDraft from free text via the model
services/api/horolog/capture.py::capture.detail: Async one-shot call to `extract` with the IntentDraft schema, the module SYSTEM prompt, and the raw text; provider is optional and falls back to `extract`'s default. Grammar-constrained output still passes through `_sane`, so ValueError propagates to the caller on an unusable draft.

services/api/horolog/api.py::CaptureIn.oneLiner: Request body: one text field, 1-2000 chars
services/api/horolog/api.py::CaptureIn.detail: Pydantic model wrapping the raw natural-language string for POST capture. Length bounds are the trust boundary — empty or oversized text is rejected with 422 before any model call.

services/api/horolog/api.py::capture_int.oneLiner: Text → LLM extraction → validated Intent row
services/api/horolog/api.py::capture_int.detail: Calls capture() to get a schema-constrained draft, converts it via to_payload(draft, origin()), then routes through the normal create_intent path so the domain model re-validates; returns {"intent": created, "understood": draft}. ExtractionFailed maps to 422, httpx transport errors to 503; writes to the DB via the injected AsyncSession but never touches a calendar directly — placement is the placer's job.

services/api/tests/test_capture.py::Scri.oneLiner: Fake LLM provider: replays canned JSON, records prompts
services/api/tests/test_capture.py::Scri.detail: Stands in for the real completion provider in tests; each `complete` call pops the next payload in order and appends the user prompt and schema to public lists. Tests assert on `prompts` to verify repair rounds happened and carried the right reason.

services/api/tests/test_capture.py::Scri.oneLiner: Stores payloads to replay and empty prompt/schema logs
services/api/tests/test_capture.py::Scri.detail: Takes payloads varargs, copies them into a mutable queue, initializes `prompts` and `schemas` to empty lists. Payload count sets the max number of calls the test allows.

services/api/tests/test_capture.py::Scri.oneLiner: Logs prompt+schema, returns next payload as JSON string
services/api/tests/test_capture.py::Scri.detail: Matches the provider protocol signature (system, user, schema, name) but ignores `system` and `name`; returns `json.dumps` of the popped payload. Popping from the front means an extra call past the scripted payloads raises IndexError — that is the intended failure signal.

services/api/tests/test_capture.py::draf.oneLiner: Builds a valid IntentDraft dict, overridable per key
services/api/tests/test_capture.py::draf.detail: Returns a baseline task payload (3h, 60–120 min chunks, due in 3 days) merged with keyword overrides. Tests override single fields to construct one specific violation at a time.

services/api/tests/test_capture.py::test.oneLiner: Checks strict_schema output meets decoder restrictions
services/api/tests/test_capture.py::test.detail: Asserts `additionalProperties: false`, every property listed in `required`, and optional fields encoded as `anyOf [T, null]` rather than omitted. Also asserts no `maxLength`/`minimum` anywhere in the schema — constrained decoding grammars reject those keywords.

services/api/tests/test_capture.py::test.oneLiner: Happy path: one provider call, enums parsed correctly
services/api/tests/test_capture.py::test.detail: Runs `capture` against a single valid payload and checks title plus coercion to `IntentKind.TASK` and `Priority.P2`. The `len(prompts) == 1` assert is the real point: a valid answer must not trigger a repair round.

services/api/tests/test_capture.py::test.oneLiner: Invalid first answer triggers one repair round that succeeds
services/api/tests/test_capture.py::test.detail: First payload has min_chunk (60) > total minutes (30) — valid JSON, rejected by the model validator; second payload is consistent. Asserts two prompts and that the repair prompt contains "rejected", i.e. the failure reason is fed back to the model.

services/api/tests/test_capture.py::test.oneLiner: Two bad answers raise ExtractionFailed, no retry loop
services/api/tests/test_capture.py::test.detail: Scripts the same invalid payload twice; `capture` must raise `ExtractionFailed` matching "repair round". Bounds retries at one so the caller can fall back to a manual form.

services/api/tests/test_capture.py::test.oneLiner: Window shorter than min chunk is rejected and repaired
services/api/tests/test_capture.py::test.detail: 600–630 (30 min) cannot hold a 60-minute chunk; repair returns 600–720 and the result keeps window_end_min 720. Asserts the repair prompt says "widen the window" so the model gets an actionable instruction, not just a rejection.

services/api/tests/test_capture.py::test.oneLiner: window_start without window_end is rejected and repaired
services/api/tests/test_capture.py::test.detail: Start set, end null triggers validation; repair prompt must contain "both be set or both null". Result is discarded — only the prompt text is asserted.

services/api/tests/test_capture.py::test.oneLiner: to_payload rounds minutes up to the 30-min slot grid
services/api/tests/test_capture.py::test.detail: 20-minute values become 30 for both minutes_per_period and min_chunk_minutes. Rounding up, not nearest/down, so a task is never under-scheduled and then marked done.

services/api/tests/test_capture.py::test.oneLiner: due_in_days becomes an absolute date relative to NOW
services/api/tests/test_capture.py::test.detail: due_in_days=3 with the fixed `NOW` fixture yields a `due` starting 2026-03-05. Asserts on the string prefix, so the time component is unconstrained.

services/api/tests/test_capture.py::test.oneLiner: due_in_days=None leaves the due key out entirely
services/api/tests/test_capture.py::test.detail: Asserts absence of the key, not a null value — downstream distinguishes "no deadline" from "deadline unset".

services/api/tests/test_capture.py::test.oneLiner: Habit fields pass capture → to_payload unchanged
services/api/tests/test_capture.py::test.detail: Single valid habit payload (period_days=7, max_per_day=1, fixed 60-min chunks, 600–960 window) checked field by field after conversion. Chunk values already sit on the grid, so nothing here is rounded.

apps/web/app/layout.tsx::RootLayout.oneLiner: Next.js App Router root layout: html shell + skip link
apps/web/app/layout.tsx::RootLayout.detail: Renders the `<html lang="en">`/`<body>` wrapper every page nests inside, takes `children` as the routed page tree. Preconnects and loads Inter + JetBrains Mono from Google Fonts CDN (blocked CDN falls back to system stack, per the comment), and prepends a visually-hidden skip link that appears on keyboard focus. Gotcha: the skip link targets `#planner`, so any page without that id breaks the jump.

apps/web/app/lib/api.ts::IntentKind.oneLiner: Union of the five block categories
apps/web/app/lib/api.ts::IntentKind.detail: String literal union: task, habit, focus, buffer, meeting. Must match the backend's enum values exactly.

apps/web/app/lib/api.ts::Priority.detail: Numeric literal union, not a plain number. 1 is highest — scheduler drops priority 4 first when time runs short.

apps/web/app/lib/api.ts::Block.oneLiner: One scheduled slot on the calendar
apps/web/app/lib/api.ts::Block.detail: start/end are ISO timestamp strings; occurrence indexes the repeat instance and chunk indexes the split within it, so one intent maps to many blocks. moved_from holds the previous start time when the solver relocated it, null otherwise.

apps/web/app/lib/api.ts::Unmet.oneLiner: Intent the solver couldn't fully schedule
apps/web/app/lib/api.ts::Unmet.detail: shortfall_minutes is the unscheduled remainder, not the total requested. Present in a plan even when complete is false.

apps/web/app/lib/api.ts::Busy.oneLiner: External blocked interval the solver works around
apps/web/app/lib/api.ts::Busy.detail: start/end ISO strings; source names the origin (calendar feed, manual). Read-only context — not something the planner can move.

apps/web/app/lib/api.ts::Plan.oneLiner: Full solver output for one scheduling run
apps/web/app/lib/api.ts::Plan.detail: blocks are placed, unmet are the leftovers, busy is the input obstacle set. complete false means unmet is non-empty; solve_ms and generated_at are diagnostics, origin identifies which trigger produced the run.

apps/web/app/lib/api.ts::Intent.detail: minutes_per_period over period_days; period_days null means one-off rather than repeating. min/max_chunk_minutes bound how the solver splits it into blocks.

apps/web/app/lib/api.ts::request.oneLiner: fetch wrapper: JSON in, typed JSON out, throws on error
apps/web/app/lib/api.ts::request.detail: Sets content-type json and merges caller headers over it, so a caller can override. Non-2xx throws Error using the body's detail field, falling back to status text if the body isn't JSON; 204 resolves to undefined cast as T, so a T-typed call can hand you undefined.

apps/web/app/lib/api.ts::minutesBetween.oneLiner: Whole minutes between two ISO timestamps
apps/web/app/lib/api.ts::minutesBetween.detail: Date.parse both, difference in ms, rounded to nearest minute. Returns NaN on unparseable input and negative if end precedes start — no validation.

apps/web/app/lib/api.ts::formatDuration.detail: Drops the hour part under 60 and the minute part when it's zero. Assumes non-negative integer input; negatives and NaN render literally.

apps/web/app/components/Glyph.tsx::Glyph.oneLiner: Renders a 20x20 inline SVG icon selected by kind
apps/web/app/components/Glyph.tsx::Glyph.detail: Looks up a prebuilt path element in the PATHS map keyed by IntentKind and drops it into an SVG scaled to `size` (default 15px). Strokes inherit text color via `currentColor`; `aria-hidden` hides it from screen readers, so pair it with a text label. Unknown `kind` renders an empty SVG rather than throwing.

apps/web/app/components/Grid.tsx::dayKey.oneLiner: Truncates an ISO timestamp to its YYYY-MM-DD date part
apps/web/app/components/Grid.tsx::dayKey.detail: String slice of the first 10 chars — no Date parsing, so it groups by the UTC date encoded in the string, not local time. If block starts are stored as UTC, blocks late in the local day can land in the wrong column.

apps/web/app/components/Grid.tsx::offset.oneLiner: ISO time → vertical pixel offset within the day column
apps/web/app/components/Grid.tsx::offset.detail: Reads local hours/minutes, subtracts the DAY_START_H baseline, scales by PX_PER_HOUR. Times before DAY_START_H yield negative offsets and render above the grid; nothing clamps them.

apps/web/app/components/Grid.tsx::clock.oneLiner: Formats an ISO timestamp as a short local clock time
apps/web/app/components/Grid.tsx::clock.detail: Uses toLocaleTimeString with the runtime's default locale ([]), e.g. "9:05 AM". Locale-dependent output differs between server and client, so it can trip hydration mismatches.

apps/web/app/components/Grid.tsx::GridPr.oneLiner: Props for Grid: days, blocks, busy events, selection
apps/web/app/components/Grid.tsx::GridPr.detail: days are Date objects for the visible columns; blocks are schedulable items, busy are external calendar events. selected is a composite block id string or null, and onSelect is the controlled-selection callback.

apps/web/app/components/Grid.tsx::Grid.oneLiner: Renders a week calendar of scheduled blocks + busy events
apps/web/app/components/Grid.tsx::Grid.detail: Buckets `blocks` and `busy` by ISO day key, positions each absolutely via offsetPx/PX_PER_HOUR inside per-day columns, and toggles selection through onSelect(id) or onSelect(null) when the selected block is clicked again. No overlap layout — concurrent items stack at identical coordinates; heights clamp to 16px (busy) / 22px (blocks), only DAY_START_H..DAY_END_H is rendered, so events outside that window position off-grid, and blocks whose moved_from differs from start get a dashed rule plus the `settle` animation class.

apps/web/app/components/CommandBar.tsx::.oneLiner: Modal quick-capture input that posts text to api.capture
apps/web/app/components/CommandBar.tsx::.detail: Props: `open` (render gate — returns null when false), `onClose`, `onCaptured` (called after a successful capture, before onClose). Autofocuses and clears error on open, clears text on close; Escape and backdrop click close it, inner click stops propagation. Submit trims the value, blocks empty/duplicate while `busy`, and on rejection shows `caught.message` or a fallback string. Gotchas: focus/clear effect only keys on `open`, so no focus trap or body scroll lock; `EXAMPLES` buttons overwrite `text` rather than append; the example list is replaced by the error block, not shown alongside.

apps/web/app/page.tsx::Planner.oneLiner: Week-grid planner page; loads plan, live-updates via SSE
apps/web/app/page.tsx::Planner.detail: Fetches the plan via api.plan() on mount and re-fetches on every "plan" event from the /api/stream EventSource; fetch failures land in an error banner instead of throwing. Local state holds week offset (days derived in VISIBLE_DAYS chunks from today at midnight), selected block id, and ⌘K/Ctrl+K command-palette open; the sidebar shows moved-block count and unmet items, both derived from plan with useMemo. Gotchas: the days memo calls new Date() at render, so it pins to whenever weekOffset last changed, not to wall-clock rollover; moved blocks are counted as moved_from set and different from start.

apps/web/app/page.tsx::Panel.oneLiner: Bordered card with uppercase heading and children
apps/web/app/page.tsx::Panel.detail: Pure presentational wrapper: takes title and children, renders a rounded/shadowed surface with the title as a small uppercase h2. No state, no side effects.

apps/web/.next/types/validator.ts::AppPa.oneLiner: Shape a page.tsx module must match for a route
apps/web/.next/types/validator.ts::AppPa.detail: Generic over the route path; `ParamMap[Route]` pins the params object for that route, wrapped in a Promise since Next 15 made params async. `default` is the page component; the optional `generateStaticParams`/`generateMetadata`/`generateViewport`/`metadata`/`viewport` mirror the exports Next allows. Return types are `any` on purpose — this only checks names and param shapes, not metadata correctness.

apps/web/.next/types/validator.ts::Layou.oneLiner: Same shape check, for layout.tsx modules
apps/web/.next/types/validator.ts::Layou.detail: Identical to AppPageConfig except `default` takes `LayoutProps<Route>`, which adds the slot children (`children`, plus any parallel-route slots) alongside params. `LayoutRoutes` is the subset of routes that actually have a layout file.

apps/web/.next/types/validator.ts::__IsE.detail: Duplicate name from the page block — the generator emits each check inside its own block scope, so the two never collide. Only the constraint differs.

apps/web/.next/types/validator.ts::__Che.oneLiner: Instantiates the layout assertion against the real module
apps/web/.next/types/validator.ts::__Che.detail: `typeof handler` here is the root `app/layout.tsx` module. Fails if the layout's props omit `children` or mistype params.

apps/web/.next/types/validator.ts::__Unu.detail: Same no-op role as the page-side one. Ignore it.

apps/web/.next/types/routes.d.ts::AppRou.oneLiner: Union of every static page route in the app
apps/web/.next/types/routes.d.ts::AppRou.detail: Next.js generates this from the app/ directory at build time; each member is a literal pathname string. Note `/api/[[...path]]` is absent — dynamic routes live in ParamMap, so AppRoutes covers only zero-param pages.

apps/web/.next/types/routes.d.ts::PageRo.oneLiner: Union of legacy pages/ router paths — none here
apps/web/.next/types/routes.d.ts::PageRo.detail: `never` means the pages/ directory is absent or empty. Anything assigned to it is a type error.

apps/web/.next/types/routes.d.ts::Layout.oneLiner: Union of paths that have a layout file
apps/web/.next/types/routes.d.ts::Layout.detail: Only the root layout at "/" exists. Used to constrain LayoutProps and LayoutSlotMap keys.

apps/web/.next/types/routes.d.ts::Redire.oneLiner: Union of redirect sources from next.config — none
apps/web/.next/types/routes.d.ts::Redire.detail: `never` because no redirects are configured. Adding a redirect in next.config regenerates this file with the source path.

apps/web/.next/types/routes.d.ts::Rewrit.oneLiner: Union of rewrite sources from next.config
apps/web/.next/types/routes.d.ts::Rewrit.detail: "/api/[[...path]]" is an optional catch-all rewrite, so /api and /api/a/b both match. Rewrites have no file in app/, which is why the path appears here but not in AppRoutes.

apps/web/.next/types/routes.d.ts::Routes.oneLiner: Every known route path in the project
apps/web/.next/types/routes.d.ts::Routes.detail: Union of all five route categories. Constrains ParamsOf and is the type Next.js uses for typed Link hrefs.

apps/web/.next/types/routes.d.ts::ParamM.oneLiner: Maps each route to its route-params object type
apps/web/.next/types/routes.d.ts::ParamM.detail: Static routes map to `{}`; the optional catch-all `/api/[[...path]]` maps to `{ path?: string[] }` — optional because `/api` with no segments matches. Used by Next's typed-routes helpers to type `params` and link hrefs; regenerated on build, so don't edit or import it directly from app code.

apps/web/.next/types/routes.d.ts::Params.oneLiner: Looks up the params object type for one route
apps/web/.next/types/routes.d.ts::Params.detail: Indexed access into ParamMap constrained to Routes. `ParamsOf<"/api/[[...path]]">` yields `{ path?: string[] }`.

apps/web/.next/types/routes.d.ts::Layout.oneLiner: Maps a layout route to its parallel-route slot names
apps/web/.next/types/routes.d.ts::Layout.detail: `never` at "/" means no @slot directories exist under app/. Feeds the mapped type in LayoutProps.

apps/web/.next/types/routes.d.ts::PagePr.oneLiner: Props type for an App Router page component
apps/web/.next/types/routes.d.ts::PagePr.detail: Both params and searchParams are Promises — await them in the component, Next.js 15 made them async. searchParams values are string, string[] (repeated keys), or undefined.

apps/web/.next/types/routes.d.ts::Layout.oneLiner: Props type for a layout component, including slots
apps/web/.next/types/routes.d.ts::Layout.detail: Intersects params (Promise) and children with one React.ReactNode prop per parallel slot. With LayoutSlotMap = never the mapped half is `{}`, so "/" layouts get only params and children.

apps/web/.next/server/app/_not-found/pag.oneLiner: Next.js server handler for the /_not-found app page
apps/web/.next/server/app/_not-found/pag.detail: Takes (req, res, ctx-with-waitUntil): prepares the request via the route module, resolves manifests, draft/bot/RSC/PPR flags, renders the app tree inside a tracing span, and returns a CachedRouteKind.APP_PAGE cache entry ({html, rscData, postponed, headers, status}) plus cacheControl, or null. Side effects: sets Vary and other response headers, ends the response with 400 on failed prepare and 404 on on-demand revalidate of an ungenerated route, and throws error code E132 if a prerendered route reports revalidate 0 at runtime; it is minified build output, so edit the source page/route module, not this.

apps/web/.next/server/app/_not-found/pag.oneLiner: Root layout: html/head/body shell plus skip link
apps/web/.next/server/app/_not-found/pag.detail: Takes {children} and returns the <html lang="en"> document with Google Fonts preconnect links and the Inter + JetBrains Mono stylesheet in <head>. First body child is a visually-hidden skip link to #planner that appears on focus, so a #planner target must exist on the page.

apps/web/.next/server/app/page.js::f.detail: Takes `{children, delay=0, className, as='div'}` and renders element `as` with opacity/translateY driven by state `h` and a 620ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) transition offset by `delay`ms. `h` is never set to true in this build, so content stays at opacity 0 — the IntersectionObserver was dropped.

apps/web/.next/server/app/page.js::M.oneLiner: Next.js server handler that renders /page per request
apps/web/.next/server/app/page.js::M.detail: Async `(req, res, ctx)`; calls `L.prepare` for buildId, query, params and manifests (400 + empty body if it fails), then resolves render mode from request meta and headers — draft mode, RSC vs prefetch RSC, bot type, PPR postponed state, on-demand revalidate. Sets `Vary`, renders through `L.render` inside an OpenTelemetry span, and returns a cache entry `{kind: APP_PAGE, html, rscData, postponed, status, segmentData}` with its cacheControl; throws E132 if a prerendered page reports `revalidate: 0` at runtime, and falls back per `parseFallbackField` (bots get BLOCKING_STATIC_RENDER) or 404s when revalidateOnlyGenerated has no existing entry.

apps/web/.next/server/app/page.js::h.oneLiner: Renders one inline SVG icon by kind key
apps/web/.next/server/app/page.js::h.detail: Takes `{kind, size=15}`, returns a 20x20-viewBox svg with `currentColor` stroke and the path set looked up from module-scope map `g[kind]`. Unknown kind renders an empty svg — no fallback; marked aria-hidden so it needs adjacent text for meaning.

apps/web/.next/server/app/page.js::i.detail: Splits minutes into hours and remainder; drops the minute part when zero and the hour part when under 60. 0 renders as 0m.

apps/web/.next/server/app/page.js::k.oneLiner: Scroll-driven calendar demo showing blocks moving
apps/web/.next/server/app/page.js::k.detail: Reads scroll progress 0..1 from `f.G(ref)` over a 280vh spacer with a sticky inner panel; derives `k` (offsite meeting fade-in, progress .24–.44) and `l` (eased block movement, progress .48–.76, cubic in-out). Renders a week grid from `g` (days) and `h` (hours, 34px rows), interpolating each block in `i` from `from` to `to` row, dashed border and glow while in motion; footer counts moved blocks as `2*(l>.5)` — hardcoded to 2, not derived from the data.

apps/web/.next/server/app/page.js::m.oneLiner: Renders the icon for a block kind
apps/web/.next/server/app/page.js::m.detail: Looks up the SVG path set in map l by kind and wraps it in a 20x20 stroked svg sized by the size prop (default 15). Decorative only: aria-hidden, no fallback if kind is missing from l.

apps/web/.next/server/app/page.js::r.oneLiner: ISO timestamp to YYYY-MM-DD day key
apps/web/.next/server/app/page.js::r.detail: First 10 characters of the string. Used to bucket blocks into day columns, so it keys by the timestamp's own offset, not local time.

apps/web/.next/server/app/page.js::s.oneLiner: Time to pixel offset in the day column
apps/web/.next/server/app/page.js::s.detail: Converts a timestamp to minutes since local midnight, subtracts 420 (7am, the grid's first row), and scales at 58px per hour. Anything before 7am or after 9pm lands outside the 812px column.

apps/web/.next/server/app/page.js::t.oneLiner: Formats a timestamp as local clock time
apps/web/.next/server/app/page.js::t.detail: toLocaleTimeString with numeric hour and 2-digit minute, using the browser locale. Locale-dependent output differs between server and client render.

apps/web/.next/server/app/page.js::u.oneLiner: Week grid: hour rows, busy plus scheduled blocks
apps/web/.next/server/app/page.js::u.detail: Draws a 14-row 7am-9pm gutter and one column per day, filtering blocks and busy by day key; busy sits at z-0 as static divs, scheduled blocks at z-10 as buttons colored by priority with a dashed left border when moved_from differs from start. Clicking a block toggles selection via onSelect (null to deselect), keyed by intent_id:occurrence:chunk; heights floor at 22px (16px for busy) and the time line only shows above 38px.

apps/web/.next/server/app/page.js::v.oneLiner: Planner page root: fetches plan, renders week
apps/web/.next/server/app/page.js::v.detail: Holds plan, error, modal open, selected block, and week offset; the g.plan fetch callback is wired only to the capture modal's onCaptured, so nothing in this code loads a plan on mount. Week arrows shift the displayed 7 days by offset but do not refetch, and total scheduled minutes plus moved-block count are memoized from the current plan.

apps/web/.next/server/app/page.js::w.detail: Bordered surface panel rendering the title as a small uppercase h2 above children. Layout only, no state.

apps/web/.next/server/chunks/611.js::e.oneLiner: isBlockedPage: page is in the blocklist
apps/web/.next/server/chunks/611.js::e.detail: Boolean membership check against `BLOCKED_PAGES` (internal paths like `/_document`, `/_app`). Exact string match, no normalization.

apps/web/.next/server/chunks/611.js::c.oneLiner: Keep only entries whose key is in the allowlist
apps/web/.next/server/chunks/611.js::c.detail: Takes an array of {key,...} objects and an array of keys; returns the filtered array. Returns undefined when the second arg is falsy — callers must handle that, it is not an empty array.

apps/web/.next/server/chunks/611.js::d.detail: Returns the cached exports for a module id, or runs the factory and caches it. If the factory throws, the half-built cache entry is deleted so a later require retries.

apps/web/.next/server/chunks/611.js::g.oneLiner: normalizePagePath: canonical page path, throws on traversal
apps/web/.next/server/chunks/611.js::g.detail: Maps `/` to `/index` and prefixes non-dynamic `/index...` paths with an extra `/index` so they can't collide, otherwise just ensures a leading slash. Then re-runs `path.posix.normalize` and throws `NormalizeError` if the result differs — the guard against `..` traversal in requested paths.

apps/web/.next/server/chunks/611.js::h.oneLiner: getSpan: reads the active span off a context
apps/web/.next/server/chunks/611.js::h.detail: Returns `context.getValue(SPAN_KEY)` or `undefined`. Pure read, no mutation.

apps/web/.next/server/chunks/611.js::f.oneLiner: getPageFiles: build-manifest asset list for a page
apps/web/.next/server/chunks/611.js::f.detail: Round-trips the page through normalize/denormalize to get the manifest key, then returns `buildManifest.pages[key]`. On a miss it logs a console warning and returns `[]` rather than throwing.

apps/web/.next/server/chunks/611.js::n.oneLiner: Babel WeakMap cache for require wildcard
apps/web/.next/server/chunks/611.js::n.detail: Generated helper returning one of two WeakMaps (one for `nodeInterop=true`, one for false), or null when WeakMap is unavailable. Reassigns itself on first call so later calls skip the setup.
